title: Genesis Primitives seal themselves after a single Invocation, making an Agent's creation and token launch unrepeatable
content:
Four sections state the same closure in near-identical language. A.6.1.1.2.2.1.1.1.4 and A.6.1.1.2.2.1.1.4: "Because the Agent Creation Primitive is deployed solely for the one-time creation of the Agent, no further Instances of the Primitive can be Invoked." A.6.1.1.2.2.1.2.1.4 and A.6.1.1.2.2.1.2.4 say the same for Prime Transformation, A.6.1.1.2.2.1.3.1.4 for Executor Transformation, and A.6.1.1.2.2.1.4.1.4 for the Agent Token Primitive.

The distinction being drawn is between **Genesis Primitives**, which fire once and then permanently close, and **Operational Primitives** (A.6.1.1.2.2.2), whose Hub Documents keep a live In Progress Invocations Directory and can be re-invoked indefinitely.

The consequence is that an Agent's constitutive facts — that it exists, what type it is, that its token was deployed — are not adjustable through the machinery that produced them. Changing them would require a different instrument entirely, which raises the cost of tampering with identity while leaving ordinary operations cheap to iterate on.

This is the same structural move the Atlas makes with Immutable versus Adaptive Documents, applied at the Agent level: fix the parts whose drift would be fatal, and leave the parts that must respond to conditions freely re-invocable.
description: The Agent Creation, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation and Agent Token Primitives each declare no further Instances can be Invoked, so identity-defining acts cannot be redone in place.
